competencies.text: Describe how PAGASA iHEAT maps help Filipinos.

days.title: PAGASA & iHEAT Maps
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe PAGASA's role, explain what the iHEAT (Heat Index and Hazard Assessment Tool) maps show, and describe how these tools help Filipinos prepare for heat-related hazards.

🌤️ Who Is PAGASA?

PAGASA stands for the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration. It is the national meteorological agency under the Department of Science and Technology (DOST).

PAGASA's main responsibilities:

  • Monitor and forecast typhoons and tropical cyclones
  • Issue rainfall, flood, and thunderstorm warnings
  • Provide heat index advisories
  • Monitor El Niño and La Niña events
  • Publish astronomical data (sunrise, sunset, tides, eclipses)
  • Maintain weather stations, radars, and satellite systems nationwide

🔥 What Is the Heat Index?

The heat index is the temperature it actually feels like to the human body — combining air temperature AND relative humidity. High humidity prevents sweat from evaporating, making you feel hotter than the actual air temperature.

Heat Index = f(Temperature, Humidity)

Heat Index RangeCategoryWhat It Means
27–32°CCautionFatigue possible with prolonged exposure and activity
33–41°CExtreme CautionHeat cramps and heat exhaustion possible
42–51°CDangerHeat cramps, exhaustion likely; heat stroke possible
52°C and aboveExtreme DangerHeat stroke imminent — emergency

🗺️ What Is the PAGASA iHEAT Map?

The iHEAT (Heat Index and Hazard Assessment Tool) is an interactive map on PAGASA's website that shows real-time and forecast heat index values across the Philippines.

How to access:

  • Visit bagong.pagasa.dost.gov.ph
  • Look for the 'Heat Index' or 'iHEAT' link
  • Select your region, province, or city
  • View current and 5-day forecast heat index

🎯 What the iHEAT Map Shows

FeatureWhat It Displays
Color-coded regionsColor reflects heat index category — green (caution) to dark red (extreme danger)
City/province heat indexClick on a region to see its current heat index value
5-day forecastPredicted heat index values for the next 5 days
AdvisoriesAlerts when heat index reaches danger levels
Historical dataComparison with past heat index records

🇵🇭 How iHEAT Maps Help Filipinos

  • Personal planning: Know the best times to go outdoors
  • School decisions: DepEd can suspend classes when heat index is dangerous
  • Worker safety: Construction, farming, and delivery workers can adjust schedules
  • Health protection: Hospitals and clinics prepare for heat-related illnesses
  • Local government planning: LGUs can open cooling centers and issue advisories
  • Agricultural planning: Farmers know when to irrigate and harvest
  • Sports and events: Athletic events can be rescheduled to cooler hours

🩺 Heat-Related Illnesses

IllnessSymptomsResponse
Heat crampsMuscle pain and spasmsRest, drink water with electrolytes, cool down
Heat exhaustionHeavy sweating, weakness, dizziness, nauseaMove to cool area, drink fluids, rest
Heat strokeHigh body temp, confusion, no sweating, faintingEmergency — call 911, cool the body immediately

🌡️ What Causes Extreme Heat Index?

  • El Niño events — warmer Pacific Ocean temperatures cause dry, hot weather in the Philippines
  • Climate change — long-term warming trends increase frequency of extreme heat days
  • Urban heat island effect — cities absorb and radiate heat from concrete and asphalt
  • High humidity — makes the body feel hotter than the actual temperature

🛡️ Heat Mitigation Strategies

StrategyWhat It Does
Stay hydratedDrink water regularly, even if not thirsty
Wear light clothingLight-colored, breathable fabrics reflect heat
Avoid peak hoursStay indoors 10 AM to 4 PM — the hottest hours
Use sun protectionHats, sunglasses, sunscreen
Urban greeningPlant trees and create green spaces to reduce heat island effect
Cooling centersLGUs establish air-conditioned public spaces during heat waves
Smart building designReflective roofs, proper insulation, natural ventilation

📌 Quick Check

  • What does PAGASA stand for? (Answer: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration)
  • What does the iHEAT map show? (Answer: real-time and forecast heat index values across the Philippines)
  • What category is a heat index of 43°C? (Answer: Danger — heat cramps/exhaustion likely, heat stroke possible)

days.title: Match Game — PAGASA Products
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each PAGASA product, heat concept, or illness to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration
Interactive tool showing real-time and forecast heat index across the Philippines
The 'feels like' temperature combining air temperature and humidity
Fatigue possible with prolonged exposure and activity
Heat cramps/exhaustion likely, heat stroke possible
Heavy sweating, weakness, dizziness, nausea — move to cool area and drink fluids
Emergency — high body temp, confusion, no sweating, fainting
Cities absorb and radiate heat from concrete and asphalt, becoming hotter than surrounding areas

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Heat Index Awareness
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: ☀️ PAGASA's iHEAT map shows a heat index of 45°C in your city today. What should you do?

choices.label: A) Avoid outdoor activity from 10 AM to 4 PM, drink water regularly, and stay in cool areas — this is Danger level
B) Go outside for a long jog
C) Wear thick, dark clothing
D) Ignore it — heat index is just a number

scenario.text: 🏫 Your school's principal sees a PAGASA advisory that heat index will reach 42°C. What should the school do?

choices.label: A) Consider suspending outdoor activities or adjusting class schedules following DepEd heat advisory guidelines
B) Hold PE class outdoors as usual
C) Turn off all fans and air-conditioning
D) Close all windows

scenario.text: 🏗️ A construction worker starts feeling dizzy and weak after hours in the sun. His skin is sweaty and his heart is racing. What is likely happening?

choices.label: A) Heat exhaustion — he should move to a cool area, drink fluids, and rest
B) He just needs a snack
C) He is having a heart attack
D) He is fine and can continue working

scenario.text: 🌳 A barangay wants to reduce the urban heat island effect in their community. What is the BEST strategy?

choices.label: A) Plant more trees, create green spaces, and use reflective or green roofs
B) Add more concrete and asphalt
C) Remove all vegetation
D) Increase the number of vehicles

scenario.text: 🌾 A farmer uses the PAGASA iHEAT forecast for the week and sees Danger-level heat on Wednesday and Thursday. What should they do?

choices.label: A) Adjust work schedules — do heavy tasks early morning or late afternoon, and rest during peak heat hours
B) Work longer hours during peak heat
C) Work without water breaks
D) Ignore the forecast

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the PAGASA Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the PAGASA Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

choices.label: A) Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration
B) Philippine Agency for General Science and Astronomy
C) Philippine Atmospheric and Geological Assessment
D) Pacific Atmospheric Group of Science Agencies

escape.text: What does the heat index measure?

choices.label: A) The 'feels like' temperature combining air temperature and humidity
B) Only air temperature
C) The temperature of the ocean
D) The temperature inside a building

escape.text: Which heat index range is categorized as DANGER?

choices.label: D) 52°C and above

escape.text: What should you do FIRST if you or someone shows signs of heat stroke (confusion, no sweating, high body temp)?

choices.label: A) Call for emergency help and cool the person's body immediately
B) Wait and see if they feel better
C) Give them coffee
D) Let them continue working

escape.text: What is the urban heat island effect?

choices.label: A) Cities are hotter than surrounding areas because concrete and asphalt absorb and radiate heat
B) Islands are always cooler than the mainland
C) Heat escapes only at night
D) Urban areas have more rain

escape.text: How can the PAGASA iHEAT map help LGUs (local government units)?

choices.label: A) By showing heat index forecasts, LGUs can open cooling centers and issue heat advisories
B) By predicting earthquakes
C) By providing traffic updates
D) By monitoring volcanoes
